title: Bedtime Screen Use Behaviors and Sleep Outcomes in Early Adolescents: A Prospective Cohort Study
authors: Nagata JM, Cheng CM, Shim J, Kiss O, Ganson KT, Testa A, He J, Baker FC

primary_models.name: Weighted logistic regression of binary total sleep disturbance (Year 3) on Year 2 bedtime phone/SM behaviors, adjusted for Year 2 sleep disturbance and sociodemographic/clinical covariates
primary_models.location_in_paper: Table 3, 'Total sleep disturbance' OR column (p. 654); Results p. 652-653; Discussion p. 653
primary_models.design: Prospective cohort, two waves. Bedtime screen behaviors measured at Year 2; sleep outcome measured at Year 3 (one year later), adjusting for the same sleep variable at Year 2. One observation per participant; no repeated-measures structure, no time interaction.
primary_models.sample: ABCD Study (release not stated in the paper), Year 2 follow-up (2018-2020) used for exposures and Year 3 (2019-2021) for outcomes. Analytic N = 9,398 participants with complete data; 2,564 of the 11,875 baseline participants were excluded (comparison of included vs. excluded in Appendix A, not bundled in the PDF). Year 2 mean age 12.02 (SD 0.66). 48.4% female, 51.6% male. Race/ethnicity: 54.9% White, 19.6% Latino/Hispanic, 15.4% Black, 5.5% Asian, 3.1% Native American, 1.4% Other. Household income: 15.9% <$25K, 19.9% $25-50K, 18.0% $50-75K, 14.2% $75-100K, 24.3% $100-200K, 7.7% >=$200K. Parent education: 17.5% high school or less, 82.5% college or more. Mean ACEs 1.84 (SD 1.70); mean CBCL depression t-score at Year 2 53.89 (SD 6.07); melatonin use at Year 2 4.4% (Table 1, p. 652). Same N printed for all Table 3 cells.
primary_models.iv: Phone/SM bedtime behaviors from the ABCD Screen Usage Around Bedtime measure, youth self-report at Year 2 (Table 2, p. 653). (a) 'What do you usually do with your phone when you are ready to go to sleep?' entered as a categorical variable: turn the phone off (reference, 54.9%), put the ringer on silent or vibrate (18.4%), leave the ringer on (11.2%), put it outside of the room where I sleep (15.5%). (b) Past-week frequency of 'Talk on the phone or text' and 'Spend time online on social media (e.g., Facebook)' while already in bed before going to sleep. Methods describe a five-point Likert scale from 1 (never) to 5 (every night), but Table 2 tabulates four categories (0, 1-2, 3-4, 5-7 nights); one coefficient per item is reported, implying the item was entered as a single ordinal/continuous term (per one-step increase), but the exact coding is not stated. Distribution: talk/text 66.7% 0 nights, 19.6% 1-2, 7.4% 3-4, 6.3% 5-7; social media 70.1%, 16.5%, 7.1%, 6.2%. (c) 'In the past week, how often have you had phone calls, text messages, or e-mails that wake you up after trying to go to sleep?' (83.8% 0, 10.6% 1-2, 3.4% 3-4, 2.2% 5-7 nights), same coding caveat. No means or SDs reported for any IV. Each exposure appears as its own row in Table 3; the paper does not state whether exposures were entered in separate models or jointly.
primary_models.dv: Total sleep disturbance at Year 3, caregiver-reported 26-item Sleep Disturbance Scale for Children (each item 1 never to 5 daily, past six months), summed and binarized at the clinical cutoff of 39. 25.5% of the analytic sample met the cutoff at Year 3 (Table 1). Year 2 binary total sleep disturbance enters as a covariate.

primary_models.equation: logit(P(SleepDisturbance_Y3[i]=1)) = b0 + b1*PhoneSM_Y2[i] (or b1a..b1c for the three phone-action dummies) + b2*SleepDisturbance_Y2 + b3*age + b4*sex + b5..b9*race/ethnicity + b10*income + b11*parent_ed + b12*ACEs + b13*CBCL_depression + b14*melatonin + b15..*site dummies; weighted by ABCD ACS propensity weights
primary_models.estimation: Stata 18 (StataCorp). ABCD propensity weights based on the American Community Survey applied. Study site entered as a covariate; no random effects or family clustering described. Significance at p < .05 (bold in Table 3); no multiple-comparison correction reported. No interaction or stratified analyses reported. Binary logistic regression; ORs with 95% CIs reported. A supplemental ordinal logistic model on the total sleep disturbance score (Appendix D) is described only narratively.

primary_models.equation: logit(P(DIMS_Y3[i] <= k)) = tau_k - (b1*PhoneSM_Y2[i] + b2*DIMS_Y2 + b3*age + b4*sex + b5..b9*race/ethnicity + b10*income + b11*parent_ed + b12*ACEs + b13*CBCL_depression + b14*melatonin + site dummies); weighted by ABCD ACS propensity weights
primary_models.estimation: Stata 18 (StataCorp). ABCD propensity weights based on the American Community Survey applied. Study site entered as a covariate; no random effects or family clustering described. Significance at p < .05 (bold in Table 3); no multiple-comparison correction reported. No interaction or stratified analyses reported. Ordered (ordinal) logistic regression. Table 3 reports the raw ordered-logit coefficient B (log-odds scale) with 95% CI, not an exponentiated OR.

d_transformation.native_metric: OR (M1); ordered-logit coefficient on log-odds scale (M2); unstandardized B in hours (M3)
d_transformation.conversion_formula: M1: d = ln(OR) * sqrt(3)/pi (Chinn 2000). M2: OR = exp(B); d = B * sqrt(3)/pi (Chinn applied to the proportional-odds OR). M3, phone-action dummies (binary contrast vs. phone off): d ~= B / SD_DV with SD_DV = 1.62. M3, frequency items: beta_std = B * SD_IV / SD_DV; d = 2*beta_std / sqrt(1 - beta_std^2) (Borenstein 2009 eq 7.1), requires SD_IV which is not reported.
d_transformation.contrast_type: Phone-action rows: each category vs. 'turn the phone off'. Talk/text, social media and woken-by-phone rows: per one-step increase on the bedtime frequency item (coding not explicitly stated; Likert 1-5 per Methods vs. 4 night-count categories in Table 2).
d_transformation.notes: M1 (OR) and M2 (ordered-logit B) convert to d without SDs. p0 for M1 = 0.255 is the Year 3 marginal rate of total sleep disturbance (Table 1, p. 652); not needed for OR conversion. SD_DV for M3 = 1.62 h (Table 1, 'Sleep duration at Year 3 (hours per night)'); M3 phone-action dummy cells convertible via B/SD_DV (uses total-sample SD in place of pooled within-group SD). M3 frequency-item cells (talk/text, social media, woken by calls/texts) are not convertible from reported statistics because the paper gives no mean/SD for the items; SD could be approximated from the Table 2 category percentages only under an assumed coding, which was not done. ABCD propensity weights used throughout. [complete-stage check 2026-10-01] Re-read full PDF (6 pp.). All 18 native values and 95% CIs present and verified against Table 3 p.654. No SEs, t/z, or exact p for '< .001' cells printed. No SD for any bedtime-frequency item (sd_iv) printed; M3 frequency cells remain non-convertible. Supplement (Appendices A-D) not bundled.

extraction_flags: 1) Which IVs count as phone/SM. I included 'Talk on the phone or text', 'Spend time online on social media', the three phone-action categories (ringer silent/vibrate, ringer on, phone outside room, each vs. turning the phone off) and 'Woken up by phone calls, text messages, or e-mails'. The phone-action and woken-by items are phone-specific but are not texting/SM time as such, so please check they belong. I excluded 'Spend time in chat rooms' (not on the FT-IC2 list, device not specified) and 'Used phone or other device when woke up during the night' (bundles other devices and mixed activities). Both are borderline; their numbers are recorded in excluded_models. 2) The IV coding is unclear. Methods describe a 1-5 Likert scale, but Table 2 shows four night-count categories, so 'per one step' is ambiguous. The paper also does not say whether each exposure was fit in its own model or entered jointly. 3) No SDs are reported for any IV, so the M3 (linear, sleep duration) frequency-item cells cannot be converted to d. The phone-action dummies are converted with B/1.62, using the total-sample SD rather than the pooled SD. 4) M2 reports raw ordered-logit coefficients (log-odds) labelled B, not ORs. I stored them in the value fields and convert them with B*sqrt(3)/pi. 5) The DV is called 'weekly sleep duration', but Table 1 gives it in hours per night (SD 1.62). 6) Appendices A-D (supplement) are not in the PDF. Appendices C and D are described only in the text, and the supplement may hold extra phone/SM numbers. 7) The ABCD release version is not stated. pdftotext drops non-bold minus signs, so every sign was checked against a 220-dpi render of Table 3. For p shown as '< .001', p is set to null and only p_label is kept.
